title: Isolation Precautions Made Simple
hook: Contact? Droplet? Airborne? One trick tells you instantly.
scenario: Patient has suspected tuberculosis. What PPE do you need BEFORE entering the room?
answer: N95 respirator + standard precautions. TB is AIRBORNE (particles <5 microns, remain suspended). NOT droplet (which requires surgical mask). Key: airborne diseases = N95; droplet = surgical mask; contact = gown + gloves.
payoff: Isolation Memory: AIRBORNE = N95 (TB, measles, chickenpox). DROPLET = surgical mask (flu, COVID, pertussis). CONTACT = gown + gloves (MRSA, C. diff).
caption:
🚨 NCLEX Trap of the Day: Isolation PPE

TB patient. What PPE?

A) Surgical mask + gown
B) N95 respirator
C) Gloves only
D) Face shield + gown

Answer: B

Airborne = N95
Droplet = Surgical mask
Contact = Gown + gloves

Remember: TB floats. It needs the GOOD mask.
